slides.title: Leadership Doesn't Require a Title
bullets: Leadership in Medical Affairs rests on competencies, not job title
These competencies can be built and shown from day one as an MSL
They are exactly what determines who advances
This final module exists to accelerate that trajectory

slides.title: Working With Diverse Stakeholders
bullets: Build trust-based relationships across internal and external stakeholders
Navigate conflicting priorities across commercial, market access, regulatory and science
Becomes leadership when used to align others around a shared medical goal

slides.title: Strategic Thinking and Business Acumen
bullets: Understand both the medical and commercial sides of the product lifecycle
Growing business knowledge supports better-informed medical decisions
The goal is not to become commercial, but to integrate the medical perspective effectively

slides.title: Influence Without Formal Authority
bullets: The most distinctive skill for medical leadership in a matrix structure
Rarely any direct hierarchical authority over the teams you coordinate with
Covered in depth in the next lesson

slides.title: Developing Others, Not Just Yourself
bullets: Effective leaders act as facilitators of their team's success
Less about personal authority, more about servant leadership
Recognized in the literature as a real competitive advantage for medical organizations

slides.title: Leadership Practiced Before It's Titled
bullets: No need to wait for a formal promotion
Every stakeholder interaction is a chance to practice leadership
Every decision that links daily work to strategy counts
Helping a colleague grow is leadership in action

takeaway.title: Medical leadership is a set of practiced competencies, not a job title
bullets: Four competencies define it: stakeholder collaboration, strategic thinking, influence without authority, and developing others
Credibility and trust remain the foundation of every one of them
These competencies can be built and demonstrated starting on day one
